title: 2009 AMC 12A Problem 20
statement: Convex quadrilateral \(ABCD\) has \(AB = 9\) and \(CD = 12.\) Diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at \(E,\) \(AC = 14,\) and \(\triangle AED\) and \(\triangle BEC\) have equal areas. What is \(AE?\)

solutions.text:
Adding \(\triangle CED\) to each of \(\triangle AED\) and \(\triangle BEC\) shows \(\triangle ACD\) and \(\triangle BCD\) have equal areas. They share base \(CD,\) so \(A\) and \(B\) are equidistant from line \(CD,\) meaning \(AB \parallel CD.\)

Then \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle CDE\) with ratio \(\dfrac{AB}{CD} = \dfrac{9}{12} = \dfrac{3}{4},\) so \(\dfrac{AE}{EC} = \dfrac{3}{4}.\)

Writing \(AE = 3x\) and \(EC = 4x,\) we get \(7x = AC = 14,\) so \(x = 2\) and \(AE = 6.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Equal areas of \(\triangle AED\) and \(\triangle BEC\) imply \(\triangle ACD\) and \(\triangle BCD\) have equal areas
That forces \(AB \parallel CD,\) making \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle CDE\) with ratio \(\dfrac{9}{12}\)
